chunks: And everything in this book that is narrated from Aban ibn Uthman has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, Ayyub ibn Nuh, Ibrahim ibn Hashim, and Muhammad ibn Abd Al-Jabbar - all of them from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Aban ibn Uthman Al-Ahmar.

key_terms.أَبَانُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ: Aban ibn Uthman, a prominent narrator
key_terms.الصَّفَّارُ: Al-Saffar, a title or nisba of a scholar
key_terms.الْأَحْمَرِ: Al-Ahmar, a descriptor meaning 'the Red' or 'the Ruddy', often used as a distinguishing epithet
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I narrated it / I transmitted it

ai.seo_question: How is the chain of narration for Aban ibn Uthman's hadiths traced in this text?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous methodology of *al-Saduq* in verifying the authenticity of narrations by explicitly tracing the *isnad* from his own teacher, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, back to Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar. It highlights the interconnectedness of the major *Thiqa* (reliable) narrators of the Kufan school, such as Muhammad ibn Abi Umair and Safwan ibn Yahya, thereby reinforcing the reliability of the transmitted knowledge within Shia hadith scholarship.
